text.p: Paul Gascoigne has issued a public apology but insisted he will not quit soccer or Glasgow Rangers despite his week of shame.
Gascoigne has been embroiled in front and back page controversy after being sent off against Ajax in a Champions' League game and allegations he assaulted his wife Sheryl.
On Friday night, the England midfieder issued a public apology to Rangers manager Walter Smith, his team mates and supporters for his ordering-off in Amsterdam.
He declared himself ready to face Aberdeen on Saturday in front of around 50,000 fans and the full media glare at Ibrox.
"There were stories about me leaving or being sacked by the club," said Gascoigne. "It's easy for me just to pack my bags and walk away from football. I ain't going to do that."
Gascoigne's only reference to the reports relating to his wife was to say that he took "a domestic problem" into Wednesday's match against Ajax, in which he was dismissed for kicking an opponent.
In his statement he said he had disgraced himself by being sent off and let everyone down.
"The thing I had -- the domestic problem -- I took that into the match with me and shouldn't have. It showed in what happened and I deeply regret what happened in Amsterdam."
The statement added: "I have to stand up for myself after what has happened and come back stronger and try and play to the best of my ability for Rangers Football Club.
"I deeply regret it. I've let down everyone at the club. I'm sure they don't need what I've given them in the last 48 hours.
"I love the club. The supporters have been great. This time last year when I let them down in a Champions' League game I came back stronger for it. Hopefully I can do that again."
Gascoigne was referring to a sending-off against Borussia Dortmund last December which was followed by his best form of the season.
Of Saturday's match, he said: "I might get the odd boos from the fans but it will take more than that to get me to give up football and walk away from this club."
Earlier, England backroom staff member Ray Clemence confirmed manager Glenn Hoddle was trying to contact Gascoigne to discuss the implications for his international career.
The troubled star is reported to have been fined two weeks' wages by Rangers, estimated at between 20,000 pounds ($31,760) and 30,000 pounds ($47,630) for his red card against Ajax.
